findings.title: V2 cleanup path throws or leaks orphan resources
findings.body: File services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java line 77 gates the RoleRemoved/ClientRemoved/GroupRemoved listener on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) only, but management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. If both features are enabled the listener runs and calls MgmtPermissionsV2.clients().setPermissionsEnabled() / roles().setPermissionsEnabled() which in ClientPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException, breaking realm/client/role/group deletion with 500. If only V2 is enabled the listener does nothing, so per-client authz Resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource are never removed on client deletion and accumulate as orphans.

findings.title: Per-client check ignores all-clients grant and can NPE
findings.body: File services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java line 207 hasPermission(ClientModel,String) looks up the per-client Resource by client.getId() and if found evaluates only that Resource. It never also evaluates the all-clients Resource (Clients). So once any per-client Resource exists (e.g. a permission created for another admin), an admin with a valid all-clients MANAGE/VIEW/CONFIGURE grant is denied for that client. Conversely, when the per-client Resource is missing it falls back to SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource() without null-checking it before calling findByResource(server,resource) on line 219, causing NullPointerException if the Clients type resource is missing.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission returns type resource name as client id
findings.body: File services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java line 138 iterates resourceStore.findByType(CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and adds resource.getName() for every granted resource. That iteration includes the aggregate type resource whose name is literally Clients created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init(). The returned Set<String> is documented/consumed as client ids/uuids, so callers receive a spurious Clients entry, causing incorrect list filtering or lookup of a non-existent client when only or also the all-clients permission is granted.

findings.title: getResourceName has no Clients branch
findings.body: File server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java line 304 getResourceName() special-cases USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE (returns All users or resolves userId to username via users().getUserById) but has no branch for CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE added in this PR. Per-client Resources are stored with name equal to client UUID and all-clients Resource with name Clients, so for Clients it falls through to resource.getDisplayName() which was never set by getOrCreateResource/init, returning null/empty instead of All clients or the clientId/client name and breaking permission/resource display and any code relying on that name.
